final_proof:
Let ψ = φ⁻¹: A₂ → A₁. Since φ is a bijection, ψ is also a bijection, and the inverse identities are φ ∘ ψ = id_{A₂} and ψ ∘ φ = id_{A₁}. It remains to prove that ψ preserves arbitrary joins and arbitrary meets.

For a subset X of Aᵢ, write ⋁ᵢX and ⋀ᵢX for its join and meet in Lᵢ, respectively. Let S ⊆ A₂ be arbitrary, and set T = ψ[S] = {ψ(s) : s ∈ S} ⊆ A₁. The identity φ(ψ(s)) = s for every s ∈ A₂ implies φ[T] = S: every element of φ[T] belongs to S, and every s ∈ S equals φ(ψ(s)), with ψ(s) ∈ T.

Because φ is a complete lattice homomorphism, it preserves the join of every subset of A₁. Hence

φ(⋁₁T) = ⋁₂φ[T] = ⋁₂S.

On the other hand, the inverse identity gives

φ(ψ(⋁₂S)) = ⋁₂S.

Thus the two elements ⋁₁T and ψ(⋁₂S) of A₁ have the same image under φ. Since φ is injective, they are equal. Recalling that T = ψ[S], we obtain

ψ(⋁₂S) = ⋁₁ψ[S].

Therefore ψ preserves the join of every subset S ⊆ A₂. The argument also applies when S is empty, so preservation of the bottom element is included.

Similarly, because φ preserves arbitrary meets and φ[T] = S,

φ(⋀₁T) = ⋀₂φ[T] = ⋀₂S.

Also,

φ(ψ(⋀₂S)) = ⋀₂S.

Injectivity of φ therefore yields

ψ(⋀₂S) = ⋀₁T = ⋀₁ψ[S].

Thus ψ preserves the meet of every subset of A₂. This includes the empty subset and hence preservation of the top element.

Consequently ψ = φ⁻¹ preserves all arbitrary joins and meets, so it is a complete lattice homomorphism. Since it is also bijective, φ⁻¹: L₂ → L₁ is a bijective complete lattice homomorphism, as claimed.
